mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility at t-0w, following a period of decline, indicates a strong rebound in consumer activity that will sustain higher retail footfall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, despite the t-0w rebound.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in TRANSIT mobility, reflecting greater public transport usage, directly correlates with increased movement throughout the metropolitan area, driving higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, even when TRANSIT mobility rises by more than 5 points for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As people shift from staying at home to returning to workplaces, indicated by rising WORKPLACES mobility and falling RESIDENTIAL mobility, they are more likely to engage in retail and recreation activities during or after their commute, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite WORKPLACES mobility rising and RESIDENTIAL mobility falling over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: The observed simultaneous rebound in RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT mobility at t-0w suggests an easing of public health restrictions or a shift in public sentiment towards greater normalcy, which will continue to drive retail and recreation activity upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show an increase, despite the initial rebound and no new policy restrictions being announced.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PARKS mobility below its baseline indicates reduced outdoor leisure activity, which, if not offset by other categories, suggests a general reduction in discretionary movement, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility falls below 20% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days, even when PARKS mobility remains below 20% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Stabilizing or slightly increasing GROCERY_PHARM mobility, following recent fluctuations, indicates a baseline level of essential movement and a return to routine, which will gradually translate into increased confidence for non-essential RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility remaining stable or increasing.

mechanism_narrative: The synchronized week-on-week increase in both RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w suggests a strong, immediate correlation between returning to work and engaging in retail activities, predicting a continued positive trend for RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES both increase week-on-week by more than 5 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 7 days, even when both RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES mobility increase by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated or increases further, it signifies a continued preference for staying at home, driven by caution or ongoing restrictions, which will suppress discretionary outings and lead to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 15% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 15% from baseline for two consecutive weeks.
